title: Influence of glutathione S-transferase polymorphisms on cognitive functioning effects induced by p,p'-DDT among preschoolers.
ehr_evidence: We used data from 326 children assessed in a prospective population-based birth cohort at the age of 4 years. In that study, the McCarthy Scales of Children's Abilities were administrated by psychologists, organochlorine compounds were measured in cord serum, and genotyping was conducted for the coding variant Ile105Val from GSTP1 and for null alleles from GSTM1 and GSTT1.
summary: In a prospective population-based birth cohort of 326 preschoolers at 4 years of age in Menorca, Spain, prenatal p,p'-DDT exposure (cord serum) was inversely associated with cognitive functioning, with effect modification by GSTP1 (but not GSTM1/GSTT1) polymorphisms.
key_findings: p,p'-DDT cord serum concentration was inversely associated with general cognitive, memory, quantitative, verbal, executive function, and working memory scores in children carrying any GSTP1 Val-105 allele, with the strongest effect being an >8-point decrement in general cognitive skills.

GSTP1 polymorphisms and prenatal p,p'-DDT exposure showed statistically significant interactions for general cognitive skills (p for interaction = 0.05), quantitative skills (p = 0.02), executive function (p = 0.01), and working memory (p = 0.02).
There were no significant associations between p,p'-DDT and cognitive functioning at 4 years according to GSTM1 and GSTT1 polymorphisms.
Adjusted associations between p,p'-DDE levels and neurodevelopmental scores were weak and not significantly modified by any of the GSTP1, GSTM1, or GSTT1 polymorphisms.
captured_features: McCarthy Scales of Children's Abilities scores (general cognitive, verbal, perceptual performance, quantitative, memory, motor, executive function, working memory)
Birth weight, birth length, gestational age
Maternal tobacco and alcohol use during pregnancy
School trimester at examination and psychologist
pathologies_diseases: Cognitive functioning/neurodevelopmental outcomes (decreased cognitive skills, executive function, working memory)
population: 326 preschoolers at 4 years of age from the Menorca cohort, Spain (recruited 1997-1999)
exposure_domain: Organochlorine pesticides (prenatal p,p'-DDT and p,p'-DDE exposure)
limitations: Selection bias possible because genotyping and exposure data were not available from all eligible children, though effects were likely minimal.
Small numbers of subjects in each subgroup limit conclusions about gene-environment interactions.
Exposure misclassification assumed to be nondifferential.
Organochlorines were not adjusted for lipid content.
Association may be secondary to linkage disequilibrium with a variant outside GSTP1.
